chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Kulayb al-Saydawi, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you promise the children, fulfill it for them, for they view you as the ones who sustain them. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not angered for anything like His anger for the women and the children.'
ai.seo_question: Why must parents fulfill promises made to their children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) emphasizes that fulfilling promises to children is crucial because they view their parents as their primary providers, a concept rooted in the Shia understanding of parental responsibility (wilayah). This specific instruction highlights the profound divine concern for the rights of women and children, distinguishing their status in Allah's eyes from other rights. The hadith serves as a practical guide for maintaining trust and spiritual integrity within the family unit.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Kulayb Al Saydawi who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When you promised the children, so fulfill it for them, for they are viewing you all as the ones who are sustaining them. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is not Angered for anything like His<sup>azwj</sup> Anger for (on behalf of) the women and the children’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Kulayb al-Saydawiy who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘When you promise children something, then you must keep your promise because they see you as the only one who provides them sustenance. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, does not become as angrier as He does for women and children.’”
